name: Antidote Pearl
flavor: Qi grinds the fang against the gland — 'the poison is its own cure, if you ask it politely' — and rolls two pearls smooth. She tests one between her teeth and nods. 'Keep them separate from the Nine Serpents. They disagree in a pouch.'

name: Nine Serpents Pill
flavor: Two glands, one seed, one plate. Qi mixes them with a bone needle in a bone cup, chanting something that is almost a song and almost a lullaby. The resulting pill is the colour of old ochre and wound with nine faint rings. 'Do not take this within a day of grief, or a day of wine.'

name: Venom-Fanged Dagger
flavor: Qi works without a forge — only a shallow basin of dark oil, a thin iron blank, and a patience that seems to live in her shoulders rather than her hands. Two fangs along the grooves, a glaze of gland-venom, eel-skin for the grip. She does not even look up. 'Re-edge it here every forty days. Or not.'

name: Nine Serpents Ring
flavor: Qi takes no spirit stones until the ring is finished — not out of kindness, she says; out of a wariness that the ring might refuse the wearer and return. The carapace is etched into nine serpents in a single evening. The lotus-seed she drops into the quench-oil; it hisses once, like a name. The ring, when she slides it over your finger, is warm.

name: Viper-Scale Sash
flavor: Qi splits the fangs to make scales — 'a fang is only a large scale that took itself too seriously' — and stitches them onto eel-skin in an overlapping pattern. The carapace-plates reinforce the spine. She smells the finished sash once and nods: 'Vinegar. Good. If it ever smells of honey, burn it.'
